_about: Models the matte sidecar can offer (matte.py reads this file; MATTE_MODELS picks ids from it). Every file is a plain ONNX graph executed by onnxruntime — no remote code. `urls` are tried in order (the pinned rembg GitHub release v0.0.0 asset first, then a mirror holding the byte-identical file); the download is verified against `sha256` before the file is used, and that sha256 is the `weights` the app folds into its memo keys. The facts come from docs/reviews/background-removal-bench/models.json (research run 2026-10-08).

isnet-anime.label: Anime (fast)
isnet-anime.upstream: SkyTNT/anime-segmentation (ISNet / DIS); the HF mirror is the author's own upload, byte-identical (same LFS sha256)
isnet-anime.notes: opset 11, input float32 [1,3,1024,1024], output [1,1,1024,1024] with the sigmoid in the graph; /255 then minus mean, std 1 (rembg dis_anime.py — NOT the ImageNet std). The 34 Resize nodes carry absolute sizes, so other input sizes are derived with tools/rescale_graph.py; fp16 on CUDA with tools/to_fp16.py (MAE 0.00005 vs fp32).

birefnet-lite.label: General (precise)
birefnet-lite.upstream: ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet, BiRefNet_lite (general-use training set, swin_v1_tiny backbone, epoch 232); rembg's ONNX export — no mirror with the same sha256 is known
birefnet-lite.notes: fixed batch 1, float32 [1,3,1024,1024] input, [1,1,1024,1024] LOGITS output (the sidecar applies the sigmoid); ImageNet mean/std. ORT's CUDA arena grows to 14.5 GB uncapped: it runs under gpu_mem_limit = MATTE_GPU_MEM_LIMIT_GIB (6.3 GB footprint at 6 GiB; 5/4/3 GiB caps FAIL). Session create 10–20 s on an RTX 5080, ~170 ms/frame; on CPU 3.7–10 s/frame at 12.6 GB RSS.
